response.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT mt.Name AS name, AVG(CAST(t.Bytes AS REAL) / t.Milliseconds) AS rate FROM Track t JOIN MediaType mt ON mt.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId WHERE t.Bytes IS NOT NULL AND t.Milliseconds <> 0 GROUP BY mt.Name) SELECT name, rate, rate / (SELECT AVG(rate) FROM r) AS rate_vs_mean FROM r

assumptions.assumption: Media types are grouped by Name, so media types that share a name form one row and count once in the mean.
The simple mean denominator covers only media type names that have at least one track with a valid ratio; names with no valid tracks are excluded rather than counted as zero.
Tracks with NULL Bytes or Milliseconds = 0 have no ratio and are skipped; the zero-milliseconds guard avoids division by zero.

alternatives.interpretation: The simple mean counts every distinct media type name in the MediaType table, treating a name with no valid ratio as a rate of 0 in the denominator.
alternatives.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT mt.Name AS name, AVG(CAST(t.Bytes AS REAL) / t.Milliseconds) AS rate FROM Track t JOIN MediaType mt ON mt.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId WHERE t.Bytes IS NOT NULL AND t.Milliseconds <> 0 GROUP BY mt.Name), names AS (SELECT DISTINCT Name AS name FROM MediaType), denom AS (SELECT AVG(COALESCE(r.rate, 0)) AS m FROM names n LEFT JOIN r ON r.name IS n.name) SELECT r.name, r.rate, r.rate / (SELECT m FROM denom) AS rate_vs_mean FROM r

alternatives.interpretation: Each media type is identified by MediaTypeId rather than by name, so two media types with the same name stay separate rows and each counts in the mean.
alternatives.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT mt.MediaTypeId AS id, mt.Name AS name, AVG(CAST(t.Bytes AS REAL) / t.Milliseconds) AS rate FROM Track t JOIN MediaType mt ON mt.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId WHERE t.Bytes IS NOT NULL AND t.Milliseconds <> 0 GROUP BY mt.MediaTypeId, mt.Name) SELECT name, rate, rate / (SELECT AVG(rate) FROM r) AS rate_vs_mean FROM r
